standards_review.notes: All 5 commit subjects in the review range use the documented EPMCDME-14403: Description format (git-workflow.md).

New code in project_service.py and application_repository.py uses modern bool | None / str | None hints; ProjectUpdateRequest's new chargeback fields follow projects.py's existing typing.Optional convention used throughout that file; the new alembic migration file is covered by the documented src/external/alembic/versions/ license-header exclusion, so no header is required.

security-patterns.md requires untrusted input be parsed strictly and rejected explicitly rather than guessed/allowed through. ProjectUpdateRequest.chargeback_attribution (projects.py:266) is a bare str with no allow-list; ProjectService._validate_chargeback_attribution (project_service.py:299-312) only validates the 'cost_center' branch, so any other value (e.g. an arbitrary string) skips validation and is written via application_repository.update_project straight into a column guarded only by the DB CheckConstraint ck_applications_chargeback_attribution (models.py:404-406). The PATCH /projects/{projectName} handler (projects.py:999-1019) does not catch IntegrityError, so a rejectable client input surfaces as an unhandled DB exception instead of a clean validation error. Authn/authz (admin-or-maintainer / project-admin check in _get_project_for_update) and the projectChargeback feature-flag gate are both correctly applied.

blocking_findings.violation: security-patterns.md's Untrusted Input Handling rule requires rejecting input that cannot be parsed/validated rather than letting it flow through; chargeback_attribution accepts any string from ProjectUpdateRequest and _validate_chargeback_attribution only checks the 'cost_center' case, so any other value bypasses application-level validation entirely.
blocking_findings.why_blocking: an invalid, client-supplied chargeback_attribution value is not rejected with a clean 400 - it reaches session.flush() in application_repository.update_project and fails only via the DB's ck_applications_chargeback_attribution CheckConstraint, which the PATCH /projects/{projectName} handler never catches, turning attacker/client-controlled bad input into an unhandled server exception.
blocking_findings.remedy: validate chargeback_attribution against the allowed set ({'project','cost_center'}) in _validate_chargeback_attribution (or constrain it with a Literal on ProjectUpdateRequest) and raise the existing ExtendedHTTPException(code=400, ...) for any other value before it reaches application_repository.update_project.
